messages:
alex: Heads-up — CI perf regression after the runtime change landed. We see ~12% tail-latency increase on text-gen workloads. Uploaded nsys + perf traces. Main hotspot looks CPU-side: tokenization + scheduler, and KV-cache miss path shows lock contention.

maria: Can you paste the folded perf output or a short stack excerpt? want to triage quickly.

alex: Pasting a trimmed folded stack from `perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl` (snipped for brevity):
```
redwood::tokenizer::tokenize; PyEval_EvalFrameEx; scheduler::dequeue; kvcache::get_or_insert; pthread_mutex_lock
redwood::tokenizer::tokenize; PyEval_EvalFrameEx; batching::compute_batch_keys; std::sort
redwood::tokenizer::tokenize; PyEval_EvalFrameEx; batching::make_batch; batch_builder::push
redwood::tokenizer::tokenize; PyEval_EvalFrameEx; kvcache::lookup_positive; pthread_mutex_lock
```
Quick notes:
- ~30% samples in `PyEval_EvalFrameEx` + `tokenize` (Python-side CPU work).
- Clear contention on `pthread_mutex_lock` inside kvcache lookup path.
- Kernel-selection heuristic runs per-request on the hot path (we're calling `should_run_kernel_selection()` inside the loop).

sam: Do we have the nsys timeline? want to confirm GPU utilization vs CPU wait.

alex: nsys timeline shows GPU kernels look fine but lots of idle gaps waiting for CPU prep. nvtx markers indicate many short kernel launches with CPU-side prep overhead. Snapshot: https://perf.redwood/snap/1842106789 (internal).

perf-bot: perf job 1842106792 finished — flamegraphs uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/1842106792/flame.svg

jakob: My guess: tokenizer is being run for each request on the main thread instead of vectorized pre-tokenize, and we forgot to hoist kernel selection out of the inner request loop. That function is cheap but called thousands of times now.

maria: Two quick experiments: (1) hoist kernel selection once per batch, (2) change kvcache miss path to accumulate missing keys and do a batched insert with a single lock hold. Can we try both?

alex: Working on a branch `perf/hoist-kernel-and-batch-kvcache`. Local synthetic load shows tail down ~8% after hoisting kernel selection and batching kvcache misses. Still running longer runs before canary.

sam: If local looks good, let's run a canary on dedicated capacity. Also add futex/mutex wait counters and maybe use `callgrind` for a repro to get deterministic call counts.

alex: Adding the perf+nsys commands I used for reproduction so folks can rerun locally: 
```
# perf flamegraph repro
perf record -F 99 -g --call-graph dwarf -o perf.data -- ./run_local_workload.sh --qps 200 --seq-len 512
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg

# nsys GPU + OS timeline
nsys profile --output=nsys_trace --trace=cuda,osrt,syscalls --sample=cpu --duration=120 ./run_local_workload.sh --qps 200
```
Also note: include `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1` and `PYTHONTRACEMALLOC=0` to minimize Python overhead during profile runs.

maria: Nice. Can you also capture `perf record -e futex_wait -a` during the run so we can quantify lock waits?

alex: Will do. Pushed an initial PR with hoist + batch kvcache but left feature flag `perf_hoist_kernels` off by default. Running canary now (started at 1842107000).

ci-bot: Canary deploy started for `perf/hoist-kernel-and-batch-kvcache` on dedicated-us-west-2 at 1842107005.

maria: :thumbsup: Keep us posted. If the canary shows improvement, we should land but also add a small unit-test that asserts `should_run_kernel_selection()` isn't invoked per-request in the hot path (sanity check).

alex: Agreed — adding a test + perf job to PR. Will upload updated flamegraphs and nsys traces once canary completes (~+10m).

sam: Also check `std::sort` allocations in `compute_batch_keys` — we saw allocations in heap profiler earlier that correlate with bursts. If sorting is the culprit we can use an insertion algorithm for small N.

alex: noted. thanks everyone — will follow up with results and links to the canary traces.
